implementation_notes: Passport is the de facto realization: each mechanism is a Strategy implementing authenticate(req, options) plus a verify callback, registered under a name with passport.use() and applied per route with passport.authenticate('name'); the resolved user is written to req.user, the normalized principal. Strategies ship as separate packages, so the mechanism set is an installation and configuration decision. A Map of verify functions keyed by scheme is the adequate hand-rolled form for a single service, and Node's crypto (scrypt, pbkdf2, timingSafeEqual) provides the primitives those verifiers need.
pitfalls: The verify callback has three distinct outcomes: cb(err) for operational failure, cb(null, false) for invalid credentials, cb(null, user) for success; collapsing err into false hides outages.
Password hashing must use an async KDF with parameters recorded per hash, and comparisons must use crypto.timingSafeEqual.
Strategy instances are module-level singletons shared across requests; per-request state must never live on them.
Passport's session option and serialize/deserialize hooks decide what is stored client-side; storing the whole user leaks fields into the session store.
